'''Yujiro Kawamata''' (born 1952) is a Japanese [[mathematician]] working
in [[algebraic geometry]].

==Career==
Kawamata completed the master's course at the [[University of Tokyo]] in 1977. He was an Assistant at the [[University of Mannheim]] from 1977 to 1979 and a [[Miller Research Fellows|Miller Fellow]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 1981 to 1983. Kawamata is now a professor at the University of Tokyo. He won the Mathematical Society of Japan Autumn award (1988) and the Japan Academy of Sciences award (1990) for his work in algebraic geometry.

==Research==
Kawamata was involved in the development of the [[minimal model program]] in the 1980s. The program aims to show that every [[algebraic variety]] is [[birational geometry|birational]] to one of an especially simple type: either a minimal model or a Fano fiber space. The [[Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing theorem]], strengthening the [[Kodaira vanishing theorem]], is a method. Building on that, Kawamata proved the basepoint-free theorem. The cone theorem and contraction theorem, central results in the theory, are the result of a joint effort by Kawamata, [[Janos Kollar|Kollár]], [[Shigefumi Mori|Mori]], [[Miles Reid|Reid]], and [[Vyacheslav Shokurov|Shokurov]].<ref>Y. Kawamata, K. Matsuda, and K. Matsuki. Introduction to the minimal model program. ''Algebraic Geometry, Sendai 1985''. North-Holland (1987), 283-360.</ref>

After Mori proved the existence of minimal models in dimension 3 in 1988, Kawamata and [[Yoichi Miyaoka|Miyaoka]] clarified the structure of minimal models by proving the [[abundance conjecture]] in dimension 3.<ref>Y. Kawamata. Abundance theorem for minimal threefolds. Invent. Math. 108 (1992), 229-246.</ref> Kawamata used analytic methods in [[Hodge theory]] to prove the [[Kodaira dimension#Application to classification|Iitaka conjecture]] over a base of dimension 1.<ref>Y. Kawamata. Kodaira dimension of algebraic fiber spaces over curves. Invent. Math. 66 (1982), 57-71.</ref>

More recently, a series of papers by Kawamata related the [[derived category]] of [[coherent sheaf|coherent sheaves]] on an algebraic variety to geometric properties in the spirit of minimal model theory.<ref>Y. Kawamata. D-equivalence and K-equivalence. J. Diff. Geom. 61 (2002), 147-171.</ref>
